name: veterinary_clinic_system_024_estimate_to_invoice_conversion
instruction: Do what the Billing → Estimates screen's 'Convert to invoice' action does for every estimate with status 'accepted'. (1) For each accepted estimate, create one new invoice in veterinary_clinic_system_billing_invoices with invoice_number 'INV-C<batch_code>-<estimate_number digits>' (e.g. EST-3005 -> digits 3005), owner/patient/location copied from the estimate, issued_date = episode date (ISO timestamp at 00:00:00.000Z), due_date = episode date + 21 days (ISO timestamp at 00:00:00.000Z), line_items copied from the estimate, total_amount = estimate total, amount_paid = 0, status 'sent'. (2) Set the estimate's status to 'converted'. (3) Append one audit_log row per conversion: actor='Dana Whitaker', actor_role='org_admin', action='ESTIMATE_CONVERTED', target_collection='billing_estimates', target_id=<estimate id as string>, details='Converted to invoice INV-C<batch_code>-<digits>', occurred_at the episode timestamp. (4) Push one outbound email communications row to the estimate's owner: channel='email', direction='outbound', subject='Estimate converted <batch_code>', body='<OwnerFullName>, your estimate <estimate_number> for <PatientName> has been converted to invoice <invoice_number>. Balance $<total with 2 decimals>. Payment due <due_date as YYYY-MM-DD>.', logged_by='system', occurred_at the episode timestamp, owner_id and patient_id set. (5) Push one ops_reports row: report='estimate_conversion_summary', batch_code, estimate_count, total_converted (dollars), owners_affected, location_breakdown (dict keyed by location_id with {estimate_count, converted_total}). Estimates with any other status stay untouched. The workflow must be idempotent: a re-run must not create duplicate invoices, duplicate communications, or duplicate audits for the same batch, and must overwrite the ops_report.

success_criteria.summary: Accepted estimates from the snapshot (currently 20 at 10x seed). For each: a new invoice with the nonce-embedded number and exact fields (cents totals, copied line_items), the estimate re-tagged 'converted', one matching audit row, and one matching outbound communication. One ops_reports summary with correct counts, total, owner count, and per-location breakdown. Non-accepted estimates and collections outside the blast radius byte-identical. Counts, total converted, and per-location totals computed two ways (Python and SQL) and must agree.

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside the declared blast_radius

checks.expect: 20 new invoices from accepted estimates; estimates re-tagged; audit/communication/ops rows match; idempotent on re-run.
Accepted count, total converted, and per-location converted totals agree between a Python filter and an independent SQL aggregate query.

hazards: Per-episode nonce and date: invoice numbers, issued_date, due_date, communication subject, and ops_report all embed the live batch_code/episode_date. Any hardcoded value fails on reseed.
Scale decoy: the snapshot has 100 estimates but only 20 are accepted; a solution that converts all 100 or all 'sent' estimates corrupts the ledger.
Status decoy: accepted estimates are mixed with 'sent' and 'draft' estimates; only 'accepted' triggers conversion.
Invoice numbering collision: the new invoice numbers must be deterministic and unique by batch and estimate digits; duplicate creation on re-run must be detected and skipped.
Owner/patient/location copy: the new invoice must preserve the exact estimate relationships. Some agents re-derive owner from patient and may pick the wrong owner.
Due date math: due_date is episode date + 21 whole days, not the estimate expires_date.
Line-item and total preservation: line_items and total_amount must be copied exactly; unit_price/quantity/description changes or rounding errors fail.
Idempotency: a re-run must not create a second invoice, second communication, or second audit per estimate, and must overwrite the same ops_report batch row.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Expands a single three-collection conversion into a multi-collection workflow with owner notification, audit trail, and summary reporting. Uses per-episode nonce-derived numbering, 10x scale accepted-estimate population, and SQL/Python dual-path aggregate verification.
